verse: Trust in the Lord, and do good; so you will dwell in the land and live securely. Delight yourself in the Lord, and he will give you your heart’s desires. (Ps 37:3-4)
When the poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue is dry with thirst, I the Lord will answer their prayers, I the God of Israel will not forsake them. (Is 41:17)

The Lord was with Joseph, and he was a man who prospered in all things. And he lived in his master’s house, who knew very well that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hands. (Gen 39:2-3)
With me, are wealth and glory, lasting riches and righteousness. For my fruit is better than gold and precious stones, and my yield better than choice silver. (Pro 8:18-19)
Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you as well. (Matt 6:33)

O afflicted one, helpless, with no one to comfort you, I will rebuild your foundations with precious stones. I will build your towers with rubies, your gates with jewels, and the wall around you with precious stones. (Is 54:11-12)
Cling to God and do not depart, and you will be prosperous at the end of your days. (Sir 2:3)
The young lions suffer want and hunger, but those who seek the Lord lack nothing good. (Ps 34:10)
The blessing of the Lord brings riches, and he adds no sorrow with it. (Pro 10:22)
My God will supply your every need according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus. (Phil 4:19)

You must be careful therefore to do as the Lord your God has commanded you; you shall not turn aside to the right or the left. You must walk in the way that the Lord your God has commanded you, so that you may live, and that it may go well with you, and that you may live long in the land that you are going to occupy. (Deut 5:32-33)
You will prosper if you carefully observe the commandments and decrees that the Lord instructed Moses concerning Israel. (1 Chron 22:13)

If you will walk in my precepts, and observe my commandments, and obey them, I will give to you rain in due season, and the ground shall bring forth its seedlings, and the trees shall be filled again with fruit. The threshing of the harvest shall last until the vintage, and the vintage shall reach unto sowing time. And you shall eat your bread to fullness, and you shall live in your land securely. (Lev 26:3-5)

If only you had paid attention to my commandments! Your prosperity would have been like a river, and your righteousness would have been like the waves of the sea, and your offspring would have been like the sand, and your descendants would have been like the grains of sand. (Is 48:18-19)

He clung to the Lord, and he did not withdraw from following him, but kept the commandments which the Lord commanded Moses. Therefore, the Lord was also with him. Wherever he went, he prospered. (2 Kgs 18:6-7)

You shall return and obey the voice of the Lord and observe all his commandments that I command you today, and the Lord your God will make you abundantly prosperous in everything you do, in your offspring, in the offspring of your livestock, and in the produce of your land. For the Lord will again rejoice in prospering you, just as he rejoiced in prospering your ancestors. (Deut 30:8-9)
You will have great wealth, if you fear God, avoid all sin, and do what is good before the Lord your God. (Tob 4:21)
If only they had such a heart in them, to fear me and keep all my commandments always, so that everything would go well with them and their descendants forever. (Deut 5:29)
Why have you transgressed the commandments of the Lord, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the Lord, he has also forsaken you. (2 Chron 24:20)

Hezekiah did what is good and upright and true before the Lord his God, for the whole service of the ministry of the house of the Lord, in accord with the law and the commandments, desiring to seek his God with his whole heart. And he did so, and he prospered. (2 Chron 31:20-21)
The Lord knows the days of the upright, and their inheritance will last forever. They will not be put to shame in an evil time; and in days of famine, they will be satisfied. (Ps 37:18-19)

During these forty years your clothes have not worn out, nor have your feet swollen up. Remember that the Lord your God disciplines you just as parents discipline their children. So then, keep the commandments of the Lord your God by walking in his ways and fearing him. (Deut 8:4-6)
The gift of God remains with the devout, and his favor will bring lasting success. (Sir 11:17)
Give your help to the poor, so that your blessing may be complete. (Sir 7:32)
Honor the Lord with your substance and give to him from the first of all your produce, and then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats shall be bursting with wine. (Pro 3:9-10)

Bring all the tithes into the storehouse and let there be food in my house. And test me about this, says the Lord, as to whether I will not open to you the floodgates of heaven, and pour out to you an abundant blessing. (Mal 3:10)

I will repay you for the years which the locust, and the hopper, and the destroyer, and the cutter consumed: my great army which I sent upon you. You will eat in plenty, and you will be satisfied, and you will praise the name of the Lord your God, who has done wonderful things for you; and my people shall never again be put to shame. (Joel 2:25-26)

The Lord has been zealous for his land, and he has taken pity on his people. And the Lord responded, and he said to his people: 'Behold, I will send you grain and wine and oil, and you will again be filled with them. And I will no longer make you a reproach among the Gentiles.' (Joel 2:18-19)

The Lord your God has blessed you in every work of your hands. The Lord your God, dwelling with you, knows your journey, how you crossed through this great wilderness over forty years, and how you have lacked nothing. (Deut 2:7)

The Lord your God is bringing you into a fertile land—a land that has rivers and springs, and underground streams gushing out into the valleys and hills; a land that produces wheat and barley, grapes, figs, pomegranates, olives, and honey; a land where you will eat bread without shortage, in which you will lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you can dig copper. (Deut 8:7)
Remember the Lord your God, it is he who gives you the power to get wealth, so that he may fulfill his covenant which he swore to your ancestors. (Deut 8:18)
I have been young, and now am old, yet I have not seen a righteous person forsaken or his children begging for bread. He is ever lending generously, and his children become a blessing. (Ps 37:25-26)

He will love you, bless you, and multiply you. He will bless the fruit of your womb, and the fruit of your land: your grain, your wine, your oil, and the increase of your herds and the young of your flock, upon the land about which he swore to your ancestors that he would give it to you. (Deut 7:13)
I will rebuke the devourer for you, so that he will not destroy the fruit of your land. Neither will the vine in the field be barren, says the Lord of hosts. (Mal 3:11)
The Lord their God will be mindful of them and bring about the restoration of their fortunes. (Zeph 2:7)
The time is coming! I will gather you; I will make you renowned and praised among all the peoples of the earth when I bring about your restoration before your very eyes, says the Lord. (Zeph 3:20)
Return to your stronghold, you prisoners of hope. Today I declare that I will restore double to you. (Zech 9:12)
God, who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed and increase the harvest of your righteousness. (2 Cor 9:10)
You will be enriched in every way so that you may be generous in every way, which will produce thanksgiving to God through us. (2 Cor 9:11)

I will restore the fortunes of my Israel. They will rebuild their ruined cities and live there; they will plant vineyards and drink the wine; they will plant gardens and eat what they grow. I will plant my people on the land I gave them, and they will not be pulled up again. (Amos 9:14-15)
I will restore them to the land which I pledged to their ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they will rule over it, and I will multiply them, and they will not be diminished. (Bar 2:34)

I will save you from all your uncleanness. And I will call for grain, and I will multiply it, and I will not impose a famine upon you. And I will multiply the fruit of the tree and the produce of the field, so that you may no longer bear the disgrace of famine among the nations. (Eze 36:29-30)
God gives the lonely a home to live in; he leads the prisoners into prosperity. (Ps 68:6)
You, O God, sent rain in abundance and you revived your inheritance when it languished. Your people settled in it; out of your goodness, O God, you provided for the poor. (Ps 68:9-10)
The Lord will send forth a blessing upon your storehouses, and upon all the works of your hands. He will bless you in the land that you shall receive. (Deut 28:8)
May the Lord give increase to you and to your children. May you be blessed by the Lord, the maker of heaven and earth. (Ps 115:14-15)
You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing. (Ps 145:16)

The Lord will open his excellent treasury, the heavens, so that it may give rain in due season and he will bless all the works of your hands. You shall lend to many nations, but you yourself will borrow nothing from anyone. (Deut 28:12)
The Lord restored Job’s fortunes when he had prayed for his friends. And the Lord gave to Job twice as much as he had before. (Job 42:10)
God is able to make every blessing abound in you, so that, always having what you need in all things, you may abound in every good work. (2 Cor 9:8)
